question: Our newsroom has a screenshot of an Alert Ready banner, but the crop cuts off the text saying where it was issued. Can I tag it as an Alberta alert based on the banner alone?
generated_answer:
No, you cannot tag it as an Alberta alert based solely on the banner. The banner does not provide enough information to determine the issuing province. You should only tag it as an Alberta alert if you have additional information confirming the province of origin. Otherwise, it should be tagged as an unknown alert. 

If you have a source that confirms the alert was issued in Alberta, please provide the source and we can update the tag accordingly. Otherwise, please do not tag it as an Alberta alert without sufficient evidence. 

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. 

Best regards, 
[Your Name]  
[Your Position]  
[Newsroom Name]  

---

**Example of a properly tagged Alert Ready screenshot:**

![Alert Ready Screenshot](https://example.com/alert-ready-alberta.png)  
**Tag:** Alert Ready (Alberta)  
**Source:** [Province of Alberta Emergency Alert System](https://www.alberta.ca/emergency-alert-system.aspx)  
**Date:** [Date of the alert]  

---

**Note:** Always verify the source and accuracy of the information before tagging or sharing Alert Ready screenshots. 

--- 

This response is based on the [Alert Ready guidelines](https://www.alertready.ca/en/guidelines/) and best practices for newsrooms handling emergency alerts.
